Peach.text: Peach Johnson is the widow of Ben, Fort Smith's dentist and mayor, and sister-in-law to Sheriff July Johnson. Nearly six feet tall, talkative and quarrelsome, she keeps pressing July to ride after Jake Spoon, the gambler who shot her husband, before he slips off to Mexico. She has no patience for a rooster that pecks her.

Joe.text: Joe Boot is Elmira's twelve-year-old son and Sheriff July Johnson's new stepson in Fort Smith, Arkansas. Skinny and big-eyed like his mother, he dodges her sharp temper alongside July, hangs around the jail like a junior deputy, fishes for catfish with Roscoe, and dreams of joining the passing cowboys, practicing with an old rope.

Elmira.text: Elmira is July Johnson's wife of four months in Fort Smith, Arkansas. Short, thin, dark-haired and impatient, she has grown cold toward her slow, steady husband and resents the idea of him chasing Jake Spoon. A few years older than July, she came from Kansas and was once married in Missouri to a man named Dee Boot.

Roscoe Brown.text: Roscoe Brown is the forty-eight-year-old deputy sheriff of Fort Smith, serving under young July Johnson. A lazy, good-natured bachelor who whittles constantly and loves dominoes, he fishes the Arkansas River with July's stepson Joe. Some blame him for letting Jake Spoon escape, and he frets about July tangling with Jake's famous Texas Ranger friends.

Dee Boot.text: Dee Boot is a gambler from Elmira's past, alive despite the smallpox story she told July. A talkative, unpredictable prankster with a small blond mustache and an old Kansas friend of Jake Spoon, he shared her wild years in Abilene and Dodge City, thinks of Joe as his boy, and staked her to a fresh start before heading north alone.

Fowler.text: Fowler is the chief trader on the whiskey boat carrying Elmira up the Arkansas River from Fort Smith. A burly former buffalo hunter with a dirty yellow beard and a twitching eyelid, he drinks day and night, scans the banks with his rifle, hates Indians, and is the only man aboard who talks to her.

Big Zwey.text: Big Zwey is a hulking buffalo hunter aboard the whiskey boat taking Elmira up the Arkansas onto the plains. With an oily beard and tar-black fingernails, he kills a trader who talked of molesting her and says he wants to marry her, though he has never spoken a word to her and only watches her from afar.

Janey.text: Janey is a skinny, barefoot runaway girl in north Texas, orphaned and passed from hand to hand until a man named Bill traded her to cruel old Sam for skunk hides. Fleeing Sam's cabin, she catches up with Roscoe Brown, treats his wasp stings with mud, catches their lunch, and rides double with him toward San Antonio.

Blue Duck.text: Blue Duck is a big, heavy-headed Comanchero bandit who rides into Lorena's camp to water his horse while Augustus McCrae bathes. Gus recalls him leading raiders who killed settlers and stole children across the Red River country, and had heard he was dead. Blue Duck threatens Gus should he ever come north of the Canadian, then rides away.

Po Campo.text: Po Campo is the Hat Creek outfit's new cook, hired by the Captain, who strolls into cow camp at dawn after a night stampede. A short, stout, white-haired old man in a holed sombrero, he refuses to ride, walks ahead of his slow donkey Maria, and befriends Newt with cheerful talk of fried grasshoppers and other odd dishes.

Ermoke.text: Ermoke leads a small band of renegade Indian raiders who meet Blue Duck and his captive Lorena at a wide red-sand river crossing. Hard-faced, with wisps of mustache at the corners of his mouth, he carries a lance hung with scalps. He and his men brutally assault Lorena, and Blue Duck has to kick him to make him stop.

Luke.text: Luke is a thin, red-headed hide hunter off the whiskey boat who helps Big Zwey carry Elmira north from Bent's Fort toward Ogallala in a battered wagon. Missing most of the fingers on one hand, with rotten teeth, a gambler's dice and a long knife, he never stops talking and brags about the Indians he claims to have killed.

Monkey John.text: Monkey John is a short, mean old white man with dirty white hair who, with his partner Dog Face, bought the captive Lorena from Blue Duck for hides. Camped on the Canadian River plains, he beats and threatens her for refusing to speak, quarrels with Dog Face, and gambles away his horses to Blue Duck.

Dog Face.text: Dog Face is a thin, scarecrow-like outlaw with wild eyes who co-owns the captive Lorena with Monkey John in a filthy camp on the Canadian. Rough but less cruel than his partner, he repeatedly stops Monkey John from hurting her and gives her a blanket. He gambles away his horses to Blue Duck and is told to help ambush Augustus.

Roy Suggs.text: Roy Suggs is one of the two younger Suggs brothers whom Jake Spoon meets in a Dallas saloon. Sullen, scraggly-bearded and cold-eyed, he keeps watching the doors and spits tobacco on the barroom floor even after the owner brings him a spittoon. He rides north toward Kansas with his brothers, Frog Lip and Jake.

Dan Suggs.text: Dan Suggs is the eldest and most talkative of the three Suggs brothers, whom Jake Spoon meets in a Dallas saloon. A cool, hard-drinking man with a mean grin, he pitches a plan to tax trail herds at Kansas river crossings and, failing that, to rob Kansas banks. He leads the group north with Jake along.

Frog Lip.text: Frog Lip is a tall Black man riding with the Suggs brothers when they leave Dallas for Kansas with Jake Spoon. He owns five guns of different calibers, spends much of his time cleaning them, and is a superb marksman, dropping a deer on the first day at a range Jake thought impossible.

Eddie Suggs.text: Eddie Suggs, usually called Ed, is one of the two younger Suggs brothers whom Jake Spoon meets in a Dallas saloon. Sullen, scraggly-bearded and always eyeing the doors, he nearly gets into a gunfight with his brother Roy over a hand of cards. He rides north toward Kansas with Dan, Roy, Frog Lip and Jake.

Sally.text: Sally is the ten-year-old elder daughter of Clara and Bob Allen, growing up on their horse ranch along the North Platte in Nebraska. Blue-eyed, sociable and thrilled by visitors, she likes bossing her little sister Betsey and proudly asks to hold the newborn boy delivered at the ranch, since she once held Betsey.

Clara.text: Clara Allen runs a horse ranch on the North Platte, twenty miles from Ogallala, nursing her husband Bob, left helpless by a horse's kick, and raising daughters Sally and Betsey. Once the most courted girl in Texas, she loves books and her piano and has buried three sons. She takes in the exhausted Elmira and tends the baby left behind.

Cholo.text: Cholo is the old Mexican cowboy, seventy-five or older, who is the only hand on Clara's Nebraska horse ranch. Wiry, cautious and devoted to Clara, he taught her to understand horses, weaves lariats from horsehair, makes the morning coffee and does the Ogallala shopping. Steady at births, he delivers Elmira's baby boy and coaxes him to breathe.

Bob Allen.text: Bob Allen is Clara's husband, a big, conventional, quiet horse trader on the North Platte in Nebraska. Three months ago a mustang mare he insisted on breaking kicked him in the head, and he now lies unable to speak or move, staring upward while Clara feeds and nurses him. He gave up whiskey years ago at her insistence.

Betsey.text: Betsey is the seven-year-old younger daughter of Clara and Bob Allen on their horse ranch along the North Platte. Brown-haired, curious and fond of company, she loves gathering eggs with her mother, wonders whether her father can hear the piano, and is delighted by the first newborn baby she has ever seen.

Martin.text: Martin is Elmira's newborn son, left at Clara's horse ranch on the North Platte when his mother hurried off to town. Clara feeds him milk through a nipple meant for colts and has named him Martin, thinking it a fine name for a future judge. When July Johnson arrives, Clara works out from the dates that the boy is his.

Patrick Arandel.text: Dr. Patrick Arandel is the Ogallala doctor who takes in Elmira, gravely ill with fever, and nurses her patiently for days. A short, red-bearded man, he is unwell himself, coughing hard, hands trembling, smelling of whiskey and living mostly on tea. He refuses her offers of payment, saying he settled there to escape money.

Old Hugh Auld.text: Old Hugh Auld is a tiny, bent old trapper in patched buckskins who finds the wounded Augustus collapsed on the Montana prairie. A former beaver trader on good terms with the Blood and Blackfeet who once scouted for Custer, he warns that Gus's rotting leg must come off, ties him onto his spotted horse, and follows him toward Miles City.

Dr. Mobley.text: Dr. Joseph C. Mobley is a small, fat, hard-drinking physician in Miles City, Montana, in a dandruff-flecked frock coat and battered bowler. He has already taken off Augustus's left leg and urgently wants to remove the other, but Gus refuses. Unwell himself, he admires the consumptive saloon girl playing piano across the street.
